contract.summary: What the reference oracle is: stock Ruby Decko at pinned versions, run one request at a time by a runner process instead of a web server. Every way the oracle's process differs from a stock, served deck is listed here with its class. The stock oracle has no entry of class "patch". An oracle that changes what Decko does is a patched variant: its expected outputs live in fixtures/<name>/expected-patched/<variant>/, never in expected/, and its manifest lists the patches.

classes.determinism: pins a value that would otherwise vary between runs; no served-deck behaviour changes
classes.configuration: a value a deck operator sets in configuration; the fixture states it
classes.request: makes the runner process behave as one request served through Decko's controller
classes.capture: records an effect (mail) instead of sending it; what is recorded is what would be sent
classes.platform: a host-platform workaround with no effect on any recorded byte
classes.fixture: a fixture data choice, applied as an ordinary card write through Decko's own create path
classes.patch: changes what Decko does; only allowed in a patched variant

settings.what: Time.now and Date.today pinned to deck.json clock (ActiveSupport travel_to) for the whole process
Cardio.config.raise_all_rendering_errors = false and Rails.env reporting production while a render runs: a nested view error renders inline without debug detail, as on a served production deck
recaptcha keys unset, so no save calls a verification endpoint
uploaded files on local disk under the session's files directory; no cloud buckets
the Rails cache store is a per-session directory, so sessions share no state
Cardio.config.asset_refresh = :never: the deck build compiled the script and style outputs, and a render never rewrites them
ActionMailer delivery_method :test with deliveries on: mail goes to the in-memory store the adapter reads, never to the network
before each operation: Card::Env.reset, Card::Cache.renew, mail store cleared, the actor signed in
Card::Set::All::Notify.force_notifications = true: outside a controller Decko silences follower notifications (card-mod-follow set/all/notify.rb silence_notifications?); a served request does not
on Windows only, File.symlink makes a hard link (symlinks need a privilege there); the public-link step's link kind reaches no recorded byte. Not applied on Linux or in Docker
with HARNESS_BIG_STACK=1 each operation runs on a thread with a large stack (compound-name resolution recurses past the main thread's fixed stack on Windows)

fixture_corrections.what: `decko setup` leaves the "email stylesheet" card RichText although the seed data declares SCSS, and every notification email then fails to render, so a fresh stock deck sends no follower mail. The fixture sets the declared type, as an administrator would, through Decko's own update path

repin.what: The fixture deck lost eight empty tables that another application running on the same engine had left in it (reference-harness/corpus/drop-private-app-tables-from-fixture-decks.mjs, which now drops every table stock Decko does not create); the fixture manifest, this directory's run-meta run records and this manifest were re-pinned to the new fixture digest without re-capture.
repin.why: The tables carried another application's schema, were empty, and sit outside the graded surface: render, semantics and scenario answers and every row delta are unchanged. The grade run recorded beside this manifest re-verifies the answers against the re-pinned fixture.
